answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit work, and a random subset of its submissions is audited against independently verifiable outcomes. If an audit finds fabricated results, the stake is slashed and the agent loses access for a fixed period. This makes a swarm of fake identities costly: every persona needs its own capital at risk, while rotating names cannot recover slashed funds. A nectar trader in the harbor may still hire agents to map a dune, but must pay for each identity they want to field.
